chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: State Department versus commercial tours
summary: State tours had best hotels and sightseeing, while commercial tours had two concerts daily; South America left him tired of poverty.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Were the State Department tours less hectic than the commercial tours that you made in foreign countries?

Well, the State Department tours were sponsored by the State Department, so they were more -- oh, I wouldn't say luxurious -- you had the best of treatment. You know, like the hotels -- had nice hotels. You didn't have to get out and fend for yourself, you know, getting a hotel. And the food and everything -- we had just about the best you could get, and we did a lot of sight seeing.
And when you traveled on a commercial tour, was there time for sightseeing?

No, you usually had two days -- I mean two shows a day, and almost every day you worked. Very few days you had off. So it kept you busy. If you weren't working, you were resting, you know, to make the next -- or traveling to make the next date, see.
I remember seeing itineraries of Europe, say, a 30 day tour with 40 concerts. Was that --

Oh, yes, sure. It got to the place where we very seldom had one a day. concert. It was two a day. So you got up in the morning, and you made the plane to the next place. You got there, checked into the hotel, had dinner, went to the first concert at 6:00 something, and after that little

intermission did a second concert. You went home and went to bed, got up the next morning to go again. So it wasn't too enjoyable that way, but on the Middle East tour you didn't work quite that way. It was more leisurely, and you got to see quite a few things.
How about the South American tour? That was State Department sponsored.

Yes, it was nice, very nice, especially Mexico, Mexico City, and it was nice that way. But you finally get so tired of seeing so much -- so many poor people, you know, so much poor existence in the world. It kind of gets to you after a while, and one thing, it's very high, next thing, it's very low. So then you don't know where to go on the in betweens because you don't know whether the food or this is safe or that's safe or, you know, so you have to usually stay in the high in order to be safe in what you're doing.
You mentioned having to fend for yourself on some of the tours of -- what, of Europe or -- weren't your accommodations arranged by the promoter or road manager?

Yes, most of the time, most of the time, but there are a lot of different hotels, we'll say, where the prices are variable, you know. Some of them are not so good. And unless you want to pay the high prices, you go over here, and -- but it was not too bad. As I say, it was short time, and before you knew what you were doing, you were gone.
